correctness.rationale: Properness confines color classes to parts; open neighborhoods are complements of parts; therefore a vertex has a uniquely occurring neighbor color exactly when another part contains a singleton color class. Requiring this for every part is exactly the condition that at least two parts witness singleton color classes. Minimizing and counting part splits yields the formula and enumerator. A direct-definition exhaustive verifier through order ten agrees on all 128 multipartite types; this finite check is only a stress test.

value.rationale: The claim is a natural complete classification on a classical dense graph family, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It converts a local uniqueness condition into a two-witness structural criterion, gives the exact chromatic number, and enumerates all optima. It also sharpens the natural general two-extra-color upper bound by locating the exact singleton-part savings.
